items.followUp: State two roles of magnesium in plant life.

rubric.why: Iron is needed for chlorophyll formation but is not part of the chlorophyll molecule.
rubric.description: Explains iron’s role in chlorophyll formation.
rubric.how: Award for stating both that iron is needed to form chlorophyll and that it is not a constituent of chlorophyll.

rubric.why: Iron is a component of cytochromes involved in electron transport.
rubric.description: Identifies another role of iron in plants.
rubric.how: Award for naming cytochromes or their role in electron transport.

modelAnswer: Iron is required for the formation of chlorophyll, although it is not a constituent of the chlorophyll molecule.
Iron is a component of cytochromes, which take part in electron transport during respiration and photosynthesis.

items.followUp: Name four factors that affect the rate of transpiration.

rubric.why: Transpiration rate is affected by environmental conditions and by plant factors.
rubric.description: Names two distinct factors affecting transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for any two different valid factors, such as light intensity, temperature, humidity, wind, soil-water availability or number of stomata.

modelAnswer: The rate of transpiration is affected by light intensity, temperature, humidity and wind or air movement.
Soil-water availability and the number of stomata can also affect the rate.

items.followUp: Describe five differences between plant cells and animal cells.

rubric.why: Prokaryotes lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus; eukaryotes have one.
rubric.description: Compares the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award for contrasting the absence of a true nucleus in prokaryotes with a membrane-bound nucleus in eukaryotes.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic DNA is generally circular, whereas eukaryotic chromosomes are linear.
rubric.description: Compares the form of genetic material.
rubric.how: Award for correctly contrasting circular prokaryotic DNA with linear eukaryotic chromosomes.

rubric.why: The two cell types characteristically have different ribosome sizes.
rubric.description: Compares ribosomes.
rubric.how: Award for stating that prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes and eukaryotes have 80S ribosomes in their cytoplasm.

rubric.why: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles, while eukaryotes possess them.
rubric.description: Compares membrane-bound organelles.
rubric.how: Award for contrasting the lack of membrane-bound organelles in prokaryotes with their presence in eukaryotes.

rubric.why: Prokaryotes divide by binary fission; eukaryotic cells divide by mitosis or meiosis.
rubric.description: Compares cell division.
rubric.how: Award for correctly contrasting binary fission with mitosis or meiosis.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotic cells have no true nucleus; eukaryotic cells have a nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.
Prokaryotic DNA is generally circular; eukaryotic chromosomes are linear.
Prokaryotic cells have 70S ribosomes; eukaryotic cells have 80S ribosomes in their cytoplasm.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have them, for example mitochondria.
Prokaryotic cells divide by binary fission; eukaryotic cells divide by mitosis or meiosis.

items.followUp: Define photosynthesis, write its equation and outline the three stages of the Calvin cycle.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis uses light energy to produce glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.description: Defines photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for describing the use of light energy to make glucose or food from carbon dioxide and water.

rubric.why: The balanced equation shows the reactants and products of photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Writes the balanced equation for photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for the balanced equation showing carbon dioxide and water yielding glucose and oxygen.

rubric.why: In carbon fixation, carbon dioxide combines with RuBP and forms PGA.
rubric.description: Describes carbon fixation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that carbon dioxide combines with RuBP to form PGA.

rubric.why: PGA is reduced to PGAL using ATP and NADPH.
rubric.description: Describes the reduction stage.
rubric.how: Award for stating that PGA is reduced to PGAL using ATP and NADPH.

rubric.why: PGAL is used to form sugars, and the remaining PGAL regenerates RuBP.
rubric.description: Describes sugar formation and regeneration of RuBP.
rubric.how: Award for stating that PGAL forms sugars and that remaining PGAL regenerates RuBP.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
6CO₂ + 6H₂O —light and chlorophyll→ C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
Carbon fixation: CO₂ combines with RuBP to form PGA.
Reduction: PGA is reduced to PGAL using ATP and NADPH.
Regeneration: Some PGAL is used to make sugars, while the remaining PGAL regenerates RuBP.

rubric.why: Enzymes are protein molecules.
rubric.description: States the chemical nature of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award for identifying enzymes as proteins.

rubric.why: Enzymes catalyse biochemical reactions and increase their rate.
rubric.description: States that enzymes act as catalysts.
rubric.how: Award for saying that enzymes are biological catalysts or that they catalyse or speed up reactions.

rubric.why: An enzyme generally acts on a particular substrate or reaction.
rubric.description: States enzyme specificity.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that enzymes are specific to their substrates or reactions.

rubric.why: Enzyme activity is affected by temperature and pH, with an optimum for each enzyme.
rubric.description: States that enzyme activity depends on conditions.
rubric.how: Award for noting an optimum temperature or pH, or that changing temperature or pH affects activity.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts and speed up biochemical reactions.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
Enzyme activity is affected by temperature and pH; each enzyme works best at an optimum temperature and pH.
Enzymes are not used up during reactions and can be reused.

items.followUp: Write a note on vitamin D, including its function and deficiency disease.

rubric.why: Ascorbic acid is the chemical name for vitamin C.
rubric.description: Identifies ascorbic acid as vitamin C.
rubric.how: Award for naming it as vitamin C.

rubric.why: Vitamin C is water soluble.
rubric.description: States its solubility.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a water-soluble vitamin.

rubric.why: Vitamin C is needed for collagen formation and supports wound healing and healthy gums.
rubric.description: Gives a function of vitamin C.
rubric.how: Award for one valid function, such as collagen formation, wound healing or maintaining healthy gums.

rubric.why: A deficiency of vitamin C causes scurvy.
rubric.description: Names the deficiency disease.
rubric.how: Award for naming scurvy as the deficiency disease.

modelAnswer: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, a water-soluble vitamin found in citrus fruits and other fresh fruits and vegetables.
It is needed for collagen formation, wound healing and healthy gums.
A deficiency of vitamin C causes scurvy, which may involve bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

items.followUp: Define the ecosystem level of biological organization.

rubric.why: The biosphere is the part of Earth where life exists.
rubric.description: Defines the biosphere as Earth’s life-supporting zone.
rubric.how: Award for describing it as the part or zone of Earth where organisms live.

rubric.why: The biosphere includes all ecosystems on Earth.
rubric.description: States what the biosphere includes.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it includes all ecosystems on Earth.

modelAnswer: The biosphere is the part of Earth where life exists.
It includes all the ecosystems on Earth and is the highest level of biological organization.
